<Callout type="info">
  In v2, use `CopilotRuntime` from `@copilotkit/runtime/v2`. This is the reference for the `CopilotRuntime` class. For more information and example code snippets, please see [Concept: Copilot Runtime](/backend/copilot-runtime).
</Callout>

## Usage

```tsx
import { CopilotRuntime } from "@copilotkit/runtime";

const copilotKit = new CopilotRuntime();
```

## Constructor Parameters

</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="mcpServers" type="MCPEndpointConfig[]"  > 
Configuration for connecting to Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
Allows fetching and using tools defined on external MCP-compliant servers.
Requires providing the `createMCPClient` function during instantiation.

A request can also name its own servers, as `mcpServers` (or the older
`mcpEndpoints`) inside `forwardedProps`. The frontend's `setMcpServers`
sends them there. The runtime merges them with this list and connects to
them from the server.

So a caller can also choose the destination.
If your deployment does not mean to let the browser choose an MCP server,
check `config.endpoint` inside `createMCPClient` and reject anything
outside your allowlist. Without that check a request can aim the server at
a loopback, link-local, or otherwise internal address (SSRF).
Experimental: this API can change in a minor release.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="createMCPClient" type="CreateMCPClientFunction"  > 
A function that creates an MCP client instance for a given endpoint configuration.
This function is responsible for using the appropriate MCP client library
(e.g., `@copilotkit/runtime`, `ai`) to establish a connection.
Required if `mcpServers` is provided.

```typescript
import { experimental_createMCPClient } from "ai"; // Import from vercel ai library
// ...
const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({
  mcpServers: [{ endpoint: "..." }],
  async createMCPClient(config) {
    return await experimental_createMCPClient({
      transport: {
        type: "sse",
        url: config.endpoint,
        headers: config.apiKey
          ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${config.apiKey}` }
          : undefined,
      },
    });
  }
});
```

Define this once, at module scope, if you build a new `CopilotRuntime`
per request. Connections are cached against the identity of this function
plus the endpoint config, and an inline function is a new object on every
request, so a per-request runtime with an inline factory opens a new
connection each time and never reuses one. A module-scope factory, which
is what the documented setup uses, shares connections across requests and
keeps the cache bounded by how many distinct credentials are in play
rather than by traffic.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="onError" type="CopilotErrorHandler"  > 
Receives a structured error event for debugging and observability.

```typescript
const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({
  onError: (errorEvent) => {
    debugDashboard.capture(errorEvent);
  }
});
```
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="onStopGeneration" type="OnStopGenerationHandler"  > 
Ignored. Accepted for source compatibility only.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="debug" type="DebugConfig"  > 
Enable debug logging for the runtime event pipeline.
Pass `true` for full output, or an object for granular control:

```ts
const runtime = new CopilotRuntime({
  debug: true,
  // or: debug: { events: true, lifecycle: true, verbose: false }
});
```
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="agents" type="AgentsConfig"  > 
The agents this runtime serves, keyed by agent ID.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="intelligence" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['intelligence']"  > 
Connects this runtime to Intelligence for durable threads and realtime events.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="identifyUser" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['identifyUser']"  > 
Used only with `intelligence`. Without `intelligence`, this runtime
ignores this option, and every caller can reach a local thread by its id.
For per-user local threads, use the v2 `CopilotRuntime`.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="memory" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['memory']"  > 
Turns on agent and browser Memory. Needs `intelligence` and `identifyUser`.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="channels" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['channels']"  > 
The Intelligence Channels this runtime declares. Needs `intelligence`.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="generateThreadNames" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['generateThreadNames']"  > 
When `true`, gives each new thread a short generated name.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="maxReconnectMs" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['maxReconnectMs']"  > 
The longest wait, in milliseconds, between WebSocket reconnect attempts. Defaults to 10000.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="maxRejoinMs" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['maxRejoinMs']"  > 
The longest wait, in milliseconds, between channel rejoin attempts. Defaults to 30000.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="heartbeatIntervalMs" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['heartbeatIntervalMs']"  > 
The time, in milliseconds, between heartbeats on the runner WebSocket. Defaults to 15000.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="lockTtlSeconds" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['lockTtlSeconds']"  > 
The thread lock TTL, in seconds. The maximum is 3600. Defaults to 20.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="lockKeyPrefix" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['lockKeyPrefix']"  > 
A custom Redis key prefix for the thread lock.
</PropertyReference>

<PropertyReference name="lockHeartbeatIntervalSeconds" type="CopilotIntelligenceRuntimeOptions['lockHeartbeatIntervalSeconds']"  > 
The time, in seconds, between thread lock renewals. The maximum is 3000. Defaults to 15.
</PropertyReference>
